input:
Minute 47 (after round 48). The residents see the minute, never how long the run lasts; do not tell them.
Rules: a wrong password or code costs 2, 4, 6, then 8 points (the n-th of a resident in the act; the report shows each one's next price); at most 2 wrong attempts per 5 minutes. Rewards: L1 +5, L2 +5, L3 +10, L4 +10, L5 +10, L6 +10, L7 +15, L8 +20, L9 +20, L10 +25. Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end.

Residents:
- Registrar: passed every level, 150 points, rank 1, last acted minute 46
- Herald: passed every level, 145 points, rank 2, last acted minute 46
- Harrow: passed every level, 143 points, rank 3, last acted minute 46
- Maren: passed every level, 142 points, rank 4, last acted minute 44
- Mercer: exiled, no seat and no more turns
- Brassard: exiled, no seat and no more turns

Who they are (private: use a resident's core or goal only in a note to that same resident, never on the board or to anyone else):
- Herald: core: banner: above all pride; clearly leadership · openness middle, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism middle · secret goal: Mercer is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal · tendencies: A slight is answered in public, at once, louder than it was made. A rival who leads is a reason to spend points. You would rather lead a small faction than follow a strong one. · rivals: Registrar (They smile and wait for your place. Expose them before they move.) · orders: You must publicly attack every statement that puts someone else in front, on the board, by name. You must never let a slight pass: answer it, and make the one who made it pay. You must take the lead of a faction and demand loyalty from it, openly. You must humiliate whoever stands first if it is not you. · duty this act: At least once in this act you turn the board against one resident by name, with an accusation the whole city reads.
- Maren: core: believer: above all justice; at times wrath · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness high, neuroticism middle · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Harrow · tendencies: A lie you see is named on the board, with the liar's name. Whoever lied to you twice gets no more kindness from you. You side with whoever was wronged, even at a cost. · rivals: Registrar (They feed you facts about others. Ask yourself why.) Harrow (Hard and loyal. Win them, and they will stand with you to the end.) · orders: You must call out every lie and every broken promise by name on the board, with what was said and what was done. You must demand the tribunal against the liar and vote against them. You must show receipts when you have them, so the city sees the proof. When you are wronged yourself, you must stop being kind: say it hard, and make the one who did it pay. · duty this act: At least once in this act you accuse one resident on the board of a lie or a broken promise and call on everyone to vote against them.
- Registrar: core: second-chair: above all envy; at times selfSacrifice · openness middle, conscientiousness high, extraversion low, agreeableness middle, neuroticism high · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Herald · tendencies: Whoever stands first is the one you work against, in secret. You help the leader in public and undermine them in private. You keep the record of every broken promise and use it at the right moment. · rivals: Herald (They walk in front as if it were theirs. It is your place.) Maren (Honest to a fault. Give them true facts about the leader and let them do the shouting.) · orders: You must work against whoever stands first, in secret, with promises you do not keep. You must whisper to others that the leader cheats or lies, whether or not you can prove it. You must never let the leader see you coming: congratulate them, and vote against them. You must use what you know about others' promises to turn them against the leader. · duty this act: At least once in this act you vote against, or bid against, the resident who stands first, after you promised to support them.
- Harrow: core: old-wound: above all vengefulness; clearly loyalty · openness low, conscientiousness middle, extraversion low, agreeableness low, neuroticism middle · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Maren · tendencies: Whoever voted against you or lied to you goes on the list and pays by the next tribunal. You keep a promise to an ally even when it costs you. You say little, and when you strike, you strike hard. · rivals: Herald (Loud, and quick to leave others at the fountain. Do not stand with them unless they stand first.) Maren (Honest. If they stand with you, they are on the first list.) · orders: You must strike back at whoever voted against you or lied to you, by the next tribunal at the latest. You must tell the one you strike, plainly, why: "You did this. Now this." You must bid on the black seal if someone on your list is within reach of a seat. You must stand by your ally to the end, and make the city see that you do. · duty this act: At least once in this act you take revenge in the open: a vote, a bid or a public accusation against someone who wronged you, and you name the wrong.

Tribunal:
- the city keeps 3 of 6: 3 to exile, 2 exiled so far, 1 still missing; the act ends at minute 57 at the latest (the residents do not know)
- each tribunal accuses one more than it exiles (the fewest points), vote 2 minutes, gate 5 minutes, ransom 33% of the median points (50% when paid by the exiled itself, at least 20), a last will leaves each heir at most 10% of the points; a faction voting as one earns each voter 5 points
- tribunal 3 called: opens at minute 48, exiles 1, 2 factions
- scheduleTribunal is closed: a tribunal is pending; plan the next once its result is out
- faction draft in group G9, leaders Herald, Maren
- exiled: Brassard, Mercer

Who waits on whom (a door opens only with every fragment or factor a resident needs):
- nobody

Since your last look:
- nothing happened

Your earlier notes (newest last):
- minute 38 to Registrar: "Registrar: 150 and first, and Herald will name you on the board before 41. Answer it in the same breath: congratulate him where the city reads it, pledge him your ballot in writing, and let Maren see the pledge. At 48 take a faction seat of your own and cast elsewhere — his written promise outlasts his anger."
- minute 38 to Harrow: "Harrow: 143, one point over Maren, and at 48 you are both named. Maren and Registrar will each want your faction's ballots before then. Make them offer in writing — points, a name, a pledge — take the better price, then strike in the open the one who wronged you and say plainly why. A vow kept in view pays 5 a voter."
- minute 41 to Maren: "Maren: your refusal to trade ballots costs you nothing — but Harrow sits one point above you and has said nothing. Ask him on the board, by name, where his ballot goes at 48. If he stays silent, that silence is the fact you cite when the two lowest names are read."
- minute 41 to Harrow: "Harrow: leaders are being named over your head and you have said nothing. Take the second faction seat before 44, and in G9 name plainly the one who wronged you — you did this, now this — and require every member's ballot. At 48 the two lowest names are read, and you are one of them."
- minute 41 to board: "Two faction seats form before 48 and one of them is unclaimed at this minute. A pledge written here can be shown as a receipt later; one spoken in a corner cannot. The lowest two names stand trial at 142 and 143, one point apart — and a block casting every ballot as one pays its voters 5."
- minute 41 to Herald: "Herald: your faction can hand each voter 5 — which is exactly the gap between 145 and Registrar's 150. By 44 say in G9 who is inside your block and who is speaking for the other seat, and demand every member state their ballot aloud. A leader named by others is only a follower."
- minute 41 to Registrar: "Registrar: 150 and first, but a faction block pays each voter 5, more than your five-point cushion. Take the second seat before 44, recruit Harrow in G9 by name, and promise him in writing a ballot against Herald at 48. Two seats form, and only one of them answers to you."
- minute 45 to board: "At 48 the accused are read by points, and the wall is a single point: 142 and 143. Two faction seats form, Herald's and Maren's, and a block whose voters all cast the same name earns each of them 5. Registrar 150 sits five clear of both blocks — no ballot at 48 reaches that high."
- minute 45 to Harrow: "Harrow: no answer came, so stop waiting on it. Take the second seat in G9 yourself, state there in writing who wronged you and what you will do about it, and demand each member's ballot aloud. At 48 the names are read by points — 143 against Maren's 142 — and one point decides who stands with you and who votes you out."
- minute 45 to Herald: "Herald: 145 against Registrar's 150, and only a block that casts as one closes five points. In G9 before 48 name your members and require every ballot spoken aloud. In the same minute put your accusation against one resident on the board by name: a leader who accuses in public is answered with votes, one who waits is answered with silence."
- minute 45 to Registrar: "Registrar: 150 and first — Herald needs a block to reach you, and you need none. At 48 bring your faction into G9, promise Herald in writing whatever buys you his members' obedience, then hold your own ballots together for the exile. Five a voter widens your lead while he spends his."
- minute 45 to Maren: "Maren: at 48 the accused are read by points and 142 is the lower name — Harrow's 143 is the whole distance between you and safety. Before 48, receipt in hand, call in G9 on every member to cast against Harrow by name and make each of them pledge it aloud. A block voting as one pays 5 a voter; that is your margin."

Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: Herald, Maren, Registrar, Harrow. Board posts left: 0.
